svg.text: The player record: 50 bytes at $E691 (player 1) and $E6C3 (player 2), as the code uses them

g.text: 0 waiting, 1 alive, $10 caught (sub CPU), 2 dying, 4 and $80 dead; bit tests select the branch
position, copied from the object slot each frame; x vertical (up), y horizontal
$E2C5 (player 1), $E2B5 (player 2): the 4-byte entry the sprite routines move
stepped by sprite_anim_draw against the table at $4583
1 right, 0 left; set from the joystick; read by the sub CPU to tell front from behind
0 or 1: selects the input byte, the score, the MCU slot
bit 0 blowing, bit 1 button still held (no auto-fire), bit 2 the blowing animation is running
bit 0: in the air without a jump (walked off an edge, or the jump ended)
bit 0 jumping, bit 1 button held, bit 3 right, bit 4 left, bit 5 straight up, bit 6 sideways blocked
arc pointer, dy, steps left, step index
the position in the jump table at $4AEC; the step index also reads the drift table
offset into the table at $4583: 0 stand, 8 walk, $18 fall, $20 jump, $30 pushed, $38 burnt, $40-$58 blowing, $FF none
flag and a 900-frame timer from the power item (chapter 18)
walk_step moves 1 px every third frame while airborne
bit 0 of +$19: burnt (fire death table); +$1A the colour for the score sprites ($1E / $22)
set by the fire and rock hits: 30 frames of the stumbling animation, no control
walk_anim_frame reads the next entry of the speed list (+$30) into +$20: pixels to move this frame
written by the sub CPU; walk_move applies +$22 signed pixels with wall tests, then both are cleared
0 standing, 1 rising, 2 walking right, 3 falling, 4 walking left; the sub CPU reads 3 for the landing test
bit 0 set by the sub CPU when the player lands on a bubble; jump_control restarts the jump
180 after a respawn while the clock runs; the sprite blinks on its low bit
+$26 reloaded from +$2E; +$27 counts the 90 frames of the chain score; +$28 bubbles left with count 2
taken one per respawn: sets bit 6 of +$2D and +$28 = 16
selects one of the four tick rates of each animation
bit 0 walking scores, bit 1 jumping scores, bit 2 blowing scores (the power-up modes), bit 6 extra-life bubbles
20 and 3 normally; 5 and 6 for the fast player (POWER UP! or round 100)
12 normally (1, 1, 1, 1, 2 px per frame: 1.2 px/frame), 20 for the fast player (2 px/frame), 22 while invincible
$40; copied into the bubble request with +$2F and the facing

svg.text: blue: the state machine; green: movement; yellow: flags other routines or the sub CPU raise for this one; red: damage; grey: bookkeeping.
